qualification: The native tasks require structural outputs and computation. A particular brand of external tool is not logically mandatory: a capable model could produce coordinates itself. For the current Qwen chat baseline, using a suitable structure/design tool is the practical route; no matched tool-ablation or measured Qwen failure is claimed.

cases.title: Predict a protein's three-dimensional structure from its sequence
cases.input: A released CAMEO2022 example is 7VRF chain A, the Drosophila Oxpecker chromodomain. The source row contains the 71-residue seqres sequence below and a 61-residue resolved seq field. Exact ProteinBench preprocessing of this row has not been independently reconstructed.
cases.required_output: A predicted three-dimensional protein structure: numerical atomic/backbone coordinates that can be compared with the experimental reference using native structural metrics such as TM-score and RMSD.
cases.why_text_answer_is_insufficient: Naming the fold or describing the protein does not supply the required coordinates. A language model can serialize coordinates in principle, but reliable folding and structural comparison require capabilities not validated in our Qwen chat baseline.
cases.tool_route: Pass the permitted sequence and prescribed sequence-alignment/template inputs to a folding model, then return its coordinate file and run structural comparison. AlphaFold2, OpenFold and ESMFold are evaluated folding models in ProteinBench; the selected model and access protocol must be recorded.
cases.tool_role: Structure predictor is the solver or solver backend; the structural comparator is a separate evaluator.
cases.case_verification_scope: Verified in the released CAMEO2022 source cohort; not a locally dispatched Qwen case, and no exact ProteinBench retained-row preprocessing is claimed.
cases.evidence_scope: native task requirement; not a measured Qwen failure

cases.title: Build a scaffold around a specified three-dimensional motif
cases.input: Official case 01_1LDB supplies the atomic coordinates of chain A residues 186–206 from lactate dehydrogenase 1LDB and specifies a 125-residue scaffold. Its released motif PDB contains the input geometry; the sequence identity of this motif is fixed.
cases.required_output: For native benchmark submission, 100 designed scaffold PDB files of the specified length, each retaining the motif geometry, plus scaffold_info.csv describing the motif placement. Evaluation assigns sequences, refolds them and compares structures.
cases.why_text_answer_is_insufficient: A proposed amino-acid string or explanation lacks the scaffold coordinates and motif placement that the benchmark accepts. The new geometry must also survive computed refolding checks; merely asserting that the design folds cannot supply those results.
cases.tool_route: Use a motif-conditioned structure generator to produce scaffold coordinates. The official evaluation then uses ProteinMPNN for sequence assignment, ESMFold for refolding, and geometric comparison; Foldseek supports clustering and novelty evaluation. AlphaFold is not the prescribed refolding tool here.
cases.tool_role: The structure generator supplies the required answer; ProteinMPNN, ESMFold and structural comparison are the native validation pipeline.
